intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: End 1990: "The 100km2 wide area air shower detector, AGASA, was completed at Akeno." (same chronology, Heisei 2).
intervals.quote: The construction of the 100km2 wide-area air shower detector, AGASA, started at the Akeno Observatory.

intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: The AGASA results page gives the data epoch of the published spectrum as "Feb. 17, 1990 -- Jul. 31, 2002". Sokolsky & Thomson give "Full operation of the array began in 1993"; Anchordoqui et al. (hep-ph/0206072) say "The full AGASA experiment has been running since 1992"; see the log.
intervals.quote: The AGASA had been in operation as the world's largest air-shower array for 13 years since 1990, but was terminated in January 2004

intervals.label: operation ended
intervals.note: Start is the termination month; observation was handed over to Telescope Array.
intervals.quote: The AGASA had been in operation as the world's largest air-shower array for 13 years since 1990, but was terminated in January 2004

name: AGASA surface and muon detector array

placements.quote: We constructed a very large surface array at the Akeno Observatory (35o 47' N, 138o 30' E)

altitude.note: Altitude of the Akeno Observatory, the centre of the array.

area.quote: AGASA covers an area of about 100 km2

station_count.quote: consists of 111 detectors on the ground (surface detectors)

summary.plain: A field of 111 scintillator panels spread over 100 square kilometres, wired together by optical fibre to catch the particle showers of the most energetic cosmic rays.
summary.technical: AGASA: 111 plastic-scintillator surface detectors (2.2 m2 each) at about 1 km spacing, 27 muon detectors under absorbers (0.5 GeV muon threshold), optical-fibre data links, central computer control; covered about 100 km2.

technology.quote: the detectors are sequentially connected with a pair of optical fibers.
technology.value: Array of plastic-scintillator surface detectors on a roughly 1 km grid, linked by optical fibres, with shielded muon detectors.
